units.literal: The encomium says: Hongyao and San Yisheng gathered round in support; Xiao He and Cao Shen lent their aid.

units.zh: 宋思顏
units.en: Song Siyan
units.literal: Song Siyan

units.zh: 東魏主不堪憂辱，詠謝靈運詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連恥。
units.en: Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.
units.literal: Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.

units.zh: 十一月，大將軍徐達及文忠等師還，車駕出勞於江上。
units.en: In the eleventh month, Grand General Xu Da, Wenzhong, and the others returned with their armies; the imperial carriage went out to welcome them on the river.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, Grand General Xu Da and Wenzhong and the others returned with their armies; the imperial carriage went out to welcome them on the river.

units.zh: 先後用陶安、汪廣洋於江西，而庭堅與王愷守浙東。
units.en: Tao An and Wang Guangyang were sent in turn to Jiangxi, while Pan and Wang Kai held eastern Zhejiang.
units.literal: In succession Tao An and Wang Guangyang were used in Jiangxi, while Tingjian and Wang Kai guarded eastern Zhe.

units.zh: 時上游諸郡次第平定，擇儒臣撫綏之。
units.en: As the upstream districts were pacified one by one, the Founder chose scholar-officials to govern and reassure them.
units.literal: At that time the various commanderies upriver were pacified in sequence; Confucian ministers were chosen to pacify and comfort them.

units.zh: 是時，遣鄧愈、湯和諸將屯陝西、彰德、汝甯、北平、永平，徙山西真定民屯鳳陽。
units.en: Generals including Deng Yu and Tang He established colonies across Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping, while people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize Fengyang.
units.literal: At this time Deng Yu, Tang He, and other generals were dispatched to colonize Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping; people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize at Fengyang.

units.zh: 六年，太僕丞樑埜仙帖木爾言：「寧夏境內及四川西南至船城，東北至塔灘，相去八百里，土膏沃，宜招集流亡屯田。」
units.en: In 1373, Liang Ye Xiantiemuer, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng and northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich; displaced persons should be recruited for garrison farming."
units.literal: In the sixth year, Liang Ye Xiantiemuer, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng, northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich and fertile; it is fitting to recruit and gather displaced persons for colony farming."

units.zh: 同時所設省中官李夢庚、郭景祥、侯元善、楊元杲、陶安、阮弘道、孔克仁、王愷、欒鳳、夏煜等數十人。
units.en: At the same time the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and dozens of others.
units.literal: At the same time officials established in the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and several tens of others.

units.zh: 郭景祥
units.en: Guo Jingxiang
units.literal: Guo Jingxiang

units.zh: 郭景祥，濠人。
units.en: Guo Jingxiang was a native of Hao.
units.literal: Guo Jingxiang was a man of Hao.

units.zh: 景祥性諒直，博涉書史，遇事敢言，太祖親信之。
units.en: Guo was sincere and upright, widely read in history, and bold in speaking his mind; the Founder trusted him personally.
units.literal: Jingxiang's nature was sincere and upright; he broadly traversed books and histories; on affairs he dared speak— the Founder personally trusted him.

units.zh: 嘗曰：「景祥文吏，而有折衝禦侮才，能盡忠於我，可大任也。」
units.en: The Founder once said, "Guo is a civil official, yet he has the talent to confront enemies and defend the realm; he can be utterly loyal to me and is fit for great responsibility."
units.literal: He once said: "Jingxiang is a civil clerk, yet has talent to repel foes and resist insult; he can exhaust loyalty to me—great charge can be given."

units.zh: 以城郭不完，輒命景祥董治之。
units.en: Because the city defenses were incomplete, the Founder repeatedly put Guo in charge of repairing them.
units.literal: Because the city walls and moats were incomplete, he would at once order Jingxiang to supervise and repair them.

units.zh: 既而和州守臣言，州城久廢，命景祥相度，即故址城之，九旬而工畢。
units.en: When the Hezhou garrison reported that the city walls had long lain in ruins, the Founder ordered Guo to survey the site and rebuild on the old foundations; the work was finished in ninety days.
units.literal: Before long the defending official of Hezhou reported that the prefectural city had long been abandoned; he ordered Jingxiang to survey and measure, and on the old site walled it—ninety days and the work was finished.

units.zh: 景祥益治城隍樓櫓，廣屯田，練士卒，威望肅然。
units.en: Guo further strengthened the walls and towers, expanded garrison farming, drilled the troops, and his authority became formidable.
units.literal: Jingxiang further repaired city walls, moats, towers, and watchtowers, expanded garrison fields, drilled soldiers and officers, and his prestige and authority were solemn.

units.zh: 與鳳陽李夢庚皆從渡江，典文書，佐謀議，分任行中書省左右司郎中。
units.en: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both crossed the Yangzi with the Founder, managed documents, assisted in planning, and served as left and right bureau directors of the branch secretariat.
units.literal: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both followed in crossing the river, managed documents, assisted in deliberation, and shared duties as Left and Right Bureau Directors of the Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 太祖以為能，授和州總制。
units.en: The Founder judged him capable and appointed him overall controller of Hezhou.
units.literal: The Founder considered him capable and appointed him Overall Controller of Hezhou.

units.zh: 仕終浙江行省參政。
units.en: He served to the end as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang branch secretariat.
units.literal: In office he ended as Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 既同調浙東分省，尋復同入為大都督府參軍。
units.en: They were later posted together to the eastern Zhe branch secretariat, then both returned as staff officers of the great military commission.
units.literal: Having been transferred together to the eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat, before long they again entered together as staff officers of the Great Military Commission.

units.zh: 先是，克滁州、太平、溧陽。
units.en: Earlier the army had taken Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang.
units.literal: Earlier, Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang had been taken.

units.zh: 和遂為重鎮。
units.en: Hezhou thus became a major stronghold.
units.literal: Hezhou thereupon became a key stronghold.

units.zh: 璽書褒勞。
units.en: The Founder sent an imperial letter of commendation.
units.literal: An imperial letter of commendation praised and comforted him.

units.zh: 明日，達率諸將上《平沙漠表》。
units.en: The next day, Xu Da led the generals in presenting the Memorial on Pacifying the Desert Sands.
units.literal: The next day, Xu Da led the generals in presenting the Memorial on Pacifying the Desert Sands.

units.zh: 皇帝儀仗：吳元年十二月辛酉，中書左相國李善長率禮官以即位禮儀進。
units.en: The emperor's ceremonial train: On the xinyou day of the twelfth month of the first Wu year, Left Chancellor Li Shanchang led the ritual officials in presenting the enthronement rites.
units.literal: The emperor's ceremonial regalia: On the xinyou day of the twelfth month of the first year of Wu, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Li Shanchang led the ritual officials in presenting the enthronement ceremonies.

units.zh: 孝康皇后常氏，開平王遇春女。
units.en: Empress Xiaokang Lady Chang was the daughter of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun.
units.literal: Empress Xiaokang Lady Chang was the daughter of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun.

units.zh: 後坐胡惟庸黨死。
units.en: Later he was executed as an associate of Hu Weiyong's faction.
units.literal: Later he was executed as a member of Hu Weiyong's faction.

units.zh: 參政張昶曰：「木輅，戎輅也，不可 以祀天。」
units.en: Participating Secretary Zhang Chang said, "The wooden carriage is the military carriage and cannot be used for sacrifice to Heaven."
units.literal: Participating Secretary Zhang Chang said, "The wooden carriage is the military carriage and may not be used to sacrifice to Heaven."

units.zh: 天子車輅：明初大朝會，則拱衛司設五輅於奉天門，玉居中，左金，次革， 右象，次木。
units.en: The Son of Heaven's state carriages: in early Ming, at great court assemblies the Imperial Guard Office arrayed the five carriages before the Gate of Receiving Heaven, with the jade carriage in the center, gold to the left, then leather, ivory to the right, then wood.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's state carriages: at the beginning of Ming, at great court assemblies the Imperial Guard Office set out the five carriages before the Gate of Receiving Heaven—jade in the center, to the left gold, next leather, to the right ivory, next wood.

units.zh: 〈（李夢庚）〉
units.en: (Li Menggeng)
units.literal: (Li Menggeng)

units.zh: 太祖怒殺部將，召諭再興，命夢庚往諸全總制軍事。
units.en: The Founder had the subordinate executed in anger, summoned Xie to admonish him, and sent Li Menggeng to Zhuquan to take overall command of the army.
units.literal: The Founder in anger killed the subordinate general, summoned and instructed Zaixing, and ordered Menggeng to go to Zhuquan as overall controller of military affairs.

units.zh: 執夢庚降於吳，夢庚死之。
units.en: They seized Li Menggeng and surrendered him to Wu; Li was put to death.
units.literal: They seized Menggeng and surrendered to Wu; Menggeng died for it.

units.zh: 再興還鎮，忿夢庚出己上，遂叛。
units.en: When Xie returned to his post, resentful that Li had been placed over him, he rebelled.
units.literal: Zaixing returned to his command, resenting that Menggeng was placed above him, and thereupon rebelled.

units.zh: 前守陳寧苛刻，人呼「陳烙鐵」。
units.en: His predecessor Chen Ning had ruled with harsh severity, and the people nicknamed him "Iron Brand Chen."
units.literal: The previous prefect Chen Ning was harsh and exacting; people called him "Iron Brand Chen."

units.zh: 五年，廷臣薦觀才，出知蘇州府。
units.en: In the fifth year court officials recommended Guan's ability, and he was appointed prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth year court ministers recommended Guan's talent, and he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.

units.zh: 郭子興 韓林兒
units.en: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er
units.literal: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er

units.zh: 郭子興
units.en: Guo Zixing
units.literal: Guo Zixing

units.zh: 郭子興，其先曹州人。
units.en: Guo Zixing's forebears were from Caozhou.
units.literal: Guo Zixing — his ancestors were men of Caozhou.

units.zh: 生三子，子興其仲出。
units.en: She bore three sons; Zixing was the middle son.
units.literal: She bore three sons; Zixing was born of her as the second son.

units.zh: 會元政亂，子興散家資，椎牛釃酒，與壯士結納。
units.en: With the Yuan regime falling into chaos, Zixing spent the family fortune—slaughtering oxen and broaching wine—to win over bold followers.
units.literal: As it happened the Yuan government was in disorder; Zixing dispersed the family wealth, slaughtered oxen and poured wine, and formed bonds with stalwart men.

units.zh: 太祖已取滁，乃遣人說均用曰：「大王窮迫時，郭公開門延納，德至厚也。
units.en: By then the future emperor had taken Chuzhou; he sent an envoy to Zhao Junyong: "When you were desperate, Lord Guo welcomed you in—his kindness was profound.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor had already taken Chu; he then sent someone to persuade Junyong, saying: "When Your Highness was in desperate straits, Lord Guo opened his gates and received you—his virtue was exceedingly great.

units.zh: 洪武三年追封子興為滁陽王，詔有司建廟，用中牢祀，復其鄰宥氏，世世守王墓。
units.en: In Hongwu year 3 (1370), Zixing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; the court built a temple and offered the middle sacrifice; the You clan of his neighborhood was restored to guard the tomb in perpetuity.
units.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; an edict ordered the officials to build a temple and sacrifice with the middle offering; his neighbor the You clan was restored, generation after generation to guard the prince's tomb.

units.zh: 至正十二年春，集少年數千人，襲據濠州。
units.en: In the spring of the Zhizheng twelfth year (1352), he rallied several thousand young men and seized Haozhou in a sudden attack.
units.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year of Zhizheng, he gathered several thousand youths and seized Haozhou by surprise.

units.zh: 始，子興同起事者孫德崖等四人，與子興而五，各稱元帥不相下。
units.en: At first Zixing and four fellow insurgents—Sun Deya among them—together with Zixing made five commanders, each styling himself marshal and refusing to yield to the others.
units.literal: At the beginning, Zixing and the four who had risen with him—Sun Deya and others—with Zixing made five; each called himself marshal and would not yield to the others.

units.zh: 父郭公，少以日者術遊定遠，言禍福輒中。
units.en: His father, known as Master Guo, traveled in his youth through Dingyuan as a practitioner of calendrical divination; his predictions of good or ill fortune always proved accurate.
units.literal: His father, known as Master Guo, in youth wandered through Dingyuan practicing the art of day-selection; when he spoke of fortune or misfortune he was invariably right.

units.zh: 子興喜，其次妻小張夫人亦指目太祖曰：「此異人也。」
units.en: Zixing was delighted, and his second wife, the younger Lady Zhang, gestured toward the future emperor and said, "This is no ordinary man."
units.literal: Zixing was pleased; his second wife, Lady Zhang the Younger, also pointing at the Founding Emperor said: "This is an extraordinary man."

units.zh: 子興三子。
units.en: Zixing had three sons.
units.literal: Zixing had three sons.

units.zh: 長子前戰死，次天敘、天爵。
units.en: The eldest had died in battle earlier; the survivors were Tianxu and Tianjue.
units.literal: The eldest son had died earlier in battle; the next were Tianxu and Tianjue.

units.zh: 有一女，小張夫人出者，事太祖為惠妃，生蜀、穀、代三王。
units.en: He had a daughter by the younger Lady Zhang who became Consort Hui to the future emperor and bore the princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.
units.literal: He had one daughter, born of the younger Lady Zhang, who served the Founding Emperor as Consort Hui and bore the three princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.

units.zh: 天爵失職怨望，久之謀不利於太祖，誅死，子興後遂絕。
units.en: Deposed and resentful, Tianjue eventually plotted against the future emperor and was executed; with him, Zixing's male line ended.
units.literal: Tianjue, having lost his post, harbored resentment; after a long while he plotted against the Founding Emperor and was executed; Zixing's line thus came to an end.

units.zh: 乃妻以所撫馬公女，是為孝慈高皇后。
units.en: He then gave him in marriage the daughter he had raised—the daughter of Master Ma—who became Empress Xiaoci the Great.
units.literal: He then gave him in marriage the daughter whom he had raised, the daughter of Master Ma — this was Empress Xiaoci the Great.

units.zh: 及長，任俠，喜賓客。
units.en: As he matured, he lived by the code of the knight-errant and loved to entertain guests.
units.literal: When he grew up, he was chivalrous and bold, and delighted in hosting guests.

units.zh: 圍解，大、均用皆自稱王，而子興及德崖等為元帥如故。
units.en: After the siege lifted, Peng Da and Zhao Junyong each proclaimed himself king, while Zixing, Deya, and the others retained the title of marshal.
units.literal: When the siege was lifted, Da and Junyong each declared himself king, while Zixing and Deya and the others remained marshals as before.

units.zh: 未幾，發病卒，歸葬滁州。
units.en: Before long he fell ill and died; his body was brought back for burial at Chuzhou.
units.literal: Before long he fell ill and died; he was buried back at Chuzhou.

units.zh: 子興奇太祖狀貌，解縛與語，收帳下。
units.en: Zixing was struck by the newcomer's striking appearance; he had him unbound, spoke with him, and took him into his service.
units.literal: Zixing was struck by the Founding Emperor's unusual appearance; he loosed his bonds and spoke with him, and took him into his personal following.

units.zh: 大有智數，子興與相厚而薄均用。
units.en: Peng Da was shrewd and capable; Zixing favored him while slighting Zhao Junyong.
units.literal: Da was greatly intelligent and resourceful; Zixing was thick friends with him but slighted Junyong.

units.zh: 均用怒，乘間執子興，幽諸德崖家。
units.en: Enraged, Junyong seized Zixing at an opportune moment and imprisoned him in Deya's house.
units.literal: Junyong was angry; seizing an opportunity he seized Zixing and confined him in Deya's house.

units.zh: 四人不悅，合謀傾子興。
units.en: The four resented this and plotted together to bring Zixing down.
units.literal: The four were displeased and together plotted to overthrow Zixing.

units.zh: 元師圍濠州，乃釋故憾，共城守五閱月。
units.en: When Yuan forces besieged Haozhou, the factions set aside old grudges and held the city together for five months.
units.literal: Yuan troops besieged Haozhou; they then released old grievances and jointly defended the city for five months.

units.zh: 子興為人梟悍善鬥，而性悻直少容。
units.en: Zixing was fierce and warlike, yet obstinate and unforgiving by nature.
units.literal: Zixing as a man was fierce and bold, skilled in fighting, yet by nature obstinate and straight, with little forbearance.

units.zh: 然有明基業，實肇于滁陽一旅。
units.en: Yet the Ming enterprise truly began with that single brigade at Chuyang.
units.literal: Yet the foundation of the Ming enterprise in truth began with that single brigade at Chuyang.

units.zh: 子興之封王祀廟，食報久長，良有以也。
units.en: That Zixing was enfeoffed as a prince, given a temple, and honored for generations was well deserved.
units.literal: Zixing's enfeoffment as prince, his temple sacrifices, and his long-lasting reward in offerings—there was good reason for all this.

units.zh: 十六年，太祖手書子興事蹟，命太常丞張來儀文其碑。
units.en: In year 16 (1383), the Hongwu Emperor wrote Zixing's life story in his own hand and commissioned Zhang Laiyi, Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, to compose the stele inscription.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Founding Emperor in his own hand wrote Zixing's deeds and ordered the Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Laiyi to compose the text for his stele.
